messages:
Sam: Quick follow-up on the memory-split ABI RFC — thanks for the reviews. Two open items I want to lock down: (1) how we surface spill/stage hints to the allocator without leaking tenant semantics, and (2) a safe migration path for pinned ranges during rollout.

Priya: For (1) my thinking is a tiny surface: Allocator.hint_spill(allocation_id, priority) + optional token for owner/quota. Keeps the allocator agnostic but lets runtime provide economics.

Ken: Concern: a plain hint() loses revocation semantics. If runtime asks to spill but another in-flight request pins the range, we race. We should model a "staged"/"pending" state so allocator can return a lease that must be honored.

Anya: We discussed epoched leases previously — that gives a clean revoke model. Lease: {id, epoch, owner_token}. Revoke increments epoch; old leases are ignored. Slight overhead but simplifies correctness.

Priya: Example API sketch:
```
// request spill intent and get a revocable lease token
Lease request_spill(AllocationId id, SpillPriority p);
// revoke by bumping epoch (from runtime side)
bool revoke_lease(Lease l);
```
Lease contains epoch and short-lived signature.

Sam: Nice. Implementing epoched leases seems safer. Quick perf note from the prototype: we saw ~12% improvement in 95th pct latency for 128-token small-batch inferences when we allowed early staging, BUT fragmentation (measured as free-frag_ratio) increased ~7% on long-running pods.

Ken: That frag bump is worrying. If fragmentation grows unbounded it'll blow OOMs or force costly compaction. We need a compaction contract on the allocator: either allocator provides a nonblocking compact_hint(range) or runtime cooperates to quiesce guests during an out-of-band compaction.

Anya: There are two trade paths: (A) do live incremental compaction (maintain forwarding tables + update guest pointers lazily), or (B) schedule full compaction during low-util windows. (A) is complex but smoother; (B) simpler but needs reliable low-util detection and could impact latency.

Priya: For correctness with KV caches: compaction must inform runtime to quiesce KV writes or remap keys. Proposed handshake:
1) runtime -> allocator: propose_compact(range_id)
2) allocator -> runtime: tentative plan + required quiesce_time
3) runtime quiesces guest modules (KV/decoder) and returns ready
4) allocator performs compaction and returns remap table
5) runtime applies remap and resumes
This keeps pointer updates explicit.

Sam: Sounds good. Who can own prototyping this? Also we should add telemetry: fragmentation_ratio, staged_count, compaction_duration, lease_revokes. Those will guard the rollout.

Ken: I'll pick up the PR for the allocator API (sketch + tests). I'll also add a config flag to enable epoched leases and live compaction hooks.

Priya: I'll add runtime-side glue (lease acquisition, revoke flow, KV quiesce integration) and a small e2e that runs mixed workloads to measure steady-state frag.

Anya: I'll write a short design doc enumerating the failure modes (race during revoke, partial remap, compaction abort) and mitigation strategies. Include required invariants for the runtime <-> allocator handshake.

Sam: Plan for rollout: feature-flagged prototype -> dogfood in dedicated pool -> canary in hosted region -> wide enable. Monitor: tail-latency, out-of-memory events, eviction-failed-rate, fragmentation_ratio. If frag_ratio > 10% above baseline for 1h, auto-disable staging.

issue-bot: created issue https://git.company/infra/3456 for allocator API + epoched-lease prototype

Sam: Perfect. Ken, Priya, Anya — please add PR links to that issue as you create them. Let's sync in the weekly arch checkin on Wednesday. :thumbsup:
